description: The GUI starts the sidecar binary and listens to its output. Beyond that only two things for the update notification: read the app's own version, and open the release page in the system browser.
_comment: Capabilities gate what the WEBVIEW may invoke over IPC - nothing else.
The sidecar is started from Rust (app.shell().sidecar() in src/main.rs),
which is a direct API call and not ACL-checked, so shell:allow-execute
and shell:allow-spawn were granting the frontend a power it never used:
the ability to run programs with arguments of its choosing. The frontend
calls invoke() on our own four commands and shell.open on one constant
URL, and builds every DOM node with textContent, so there is no known way
to reach them today - which is the point. A permission that is not needed
is one that cannot be misused later.
If Start ever stops working after a Tauri upgrade, this is the first
place to look: add shell:allow-spawn back with the allowlist below.
